notes: Placed at a unique basal position in the 237-accession nuclear framework and described there as white-petaled.

Used as a red-flowered TE-absent comparator in MYB60 regulatory assays. Anthocyanins are described as the main chromogenic compounds for red/pink Camellia, but retain provisional taxon-specific chemistry status unless a direct assay source is linked.
MYB60-associated TIR insertion increases MYB60 expression and experimentally suppresses anthocyanin; yellow pigment identity itself is not coded from this experiment.

molecular_mechanism_evidence: CnFLS1 and CnFLS2 functional evidence; JA-CnFLS2 module
notes: HPLC/transcriptome evidence shows both flavonol glycosides and carotenoids contribute to golden-yellow petals. This is the key reason to model yellow pigments on separate axes.

molecular_mechanism_evidence: WRKY23 activates FLS and promotes flavonol accumulation
notes: Near telomere-to-telomere phased genome and functional WRKY23-FLS evidence make this a second yellow mechanism reference independent of C. nitidissima.
Clusters with C. flava, C. krempfii and C. vidalii in a lineage distinct from the main yellow-Camellia clade; a strong test of repeated recruitment versus retained ancestral deployment.
Follows the same distinct yellow trajectory as C. cucphuongensis in the 79-accession study; chemistry must be added before assigning a yellow pigment mechanism.
